mach_port_names: Takes the IPC-space read lock, sizes two page-rounded output arrays against the current entry table, drops the lock to allocate, and retries if the table outgrows them. It walks nonempty entries with generation-bearing names and a port-death timestamp, then zeroes padding and converts the used buffers into `vm_map_copy` objects for out-of-line reply delivery. Empty results free the buffers and return null copies. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L220).
mach_port_type: Special-cases NULL and DEAD names, then obtains a writable namespace lookup because `ipc_right_info` may reconcile a dead port with the entry. Returns the combined right-type bits, with the send-possible notification bits explicitly masked for compatibility. The result describes this space's rights under that name, not a unique global port identity. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L402).
mach_port_rename: This historical declaration is skipped by the kernel-server profile and has no same-symbol receiver in the indexed implementation. It must not be interpreted as a working rename operation in the current kobject dispatch table. Use the per-profile declaration and reserved-slot evidence below.
mach_port_allocate_name: Sets `qos.name`, rejects invalid requested names, and delegates to `mach_port_allocate_full`. Receive-port and port-set cases use their named allocators. The DEAD_NAME case instead calls `ipc_object_alloc_dead`, whose `ipc_entry_alloc` chooses a fresh entry and overwrites the local name variable; this wrapper does not return that replacement name. Thus the historical requested-name contract does not describe that branch. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L478), [dead-name allocator](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_object.c#L381).
mach_port_allocate: Initializes an empty QoS request and invokes `mach_port_allocate_full` with a null prototype. The selected allocator chooses a free namespace entry/name; successful receive-port or port-set allocation returns a locked object which the common allocator unlocks before returning. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L514).
mach_port_allocate_qos: Rejects the `name` option because this entry chooses the name, then shares the full allocator. Historical preallocation flags undergo size/right checks but are cleared rather than creating preallocated messages. The effective behavior therefore follows the present implementation, not the older QoS description. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L547).
mach_port_allocate_full: Validates the space, null prototype and any explicit name; preserves old preallocation errors while clearing that request. RECEIVE and PORT_SET select named or unnamed allocators according to `qos.name`. DEAD_NAME always uses `ipc_object_alloc_dead`, which chooses a fresh namespace entry rather than honoring the supplied name. Other right kinds are invalid: this routine does not manufacture a send right without a receive endpoint. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L588).
mach_port_destroy: Treats NULL/DEAD names as successful no-ops; otherwise looks up and write-locks the namespace entry and hands it to `ipc_right_destroy`, which unlocks the space. Destruction concerns all rights represented by that entry and can initiate port death/notifications when receive ownership is destroyed. Lookup failure can also record a guard exception. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L692).
mach_port_deallocate: Calls `mach_port_deallocate_kernel` with `IOT_ANY`. After a writable entry lookup, `ipc_right_dealloc` removes one applicable user reference and performs final-right/name cleanup when required. This differs from destroying every right at the entry. NULL/DEAD names succeed without lookup; invalid live names can trigger a guard exception. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L728).
mach_port_get_refs: Checks the requested right kind, resolves current type and user-reference count with `ipc_right_info`, and returns zero when the name exists but lacks that kind. Receive, port-set and send-once rights report one; send/dead-name rights use the stored urefs. Special NULL/DEAD send/send-once queries are handled before namespace lookup. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L800).
mach_port_mod_refs: Validates the requested right kind and special names, obtains a writable entry lookup and calls `ipc_right_delta`. The lower operation enforces right-specific delta, overflow, destruction and guard rules and releases the namespace lock. This changes urefs/right ownership, not the raw reference count of `ipc_port` storage. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L889).
mach_port_peek: Validates the requested trailer extent against the caller's capacity and refuses fields beyond the audit trailer, then translates the receive right. With the port queue locked, `ipc_mqueue_peek_locked` selects a queued message and reports its sequence, size, ID and trailer without receiving it. A missing matching message returns failure; no rights or message ownership transfer occurs. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L966).
mach_port_set_mscount: Translates the name as a receive right, writes `ip_mscount` under the port queue lock and unlocks. The value is the make-send generation used by notification semantics; this operation does not create send rights or change their user references. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1041).
mach_port_set_seqno: Requires a valid receive right and calls `ipc_mqueue_set_seqno_locked` while the port queue is locked. It changes receive sequencing metadata, then releases the lock; it neither dequeues nor reorders a message. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1083).
mach_port_get_set_status_from_user: Converts the destination to a referenced readable IPC space, then enumerates the selected port-set waitq membership. The helper allocates a buffer outside the object lock and retries if it is too small, sorts member names, zeroes padding, and returns a `vm_map_copy` array. The wrapper releases the space reference on return. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1361).
mach_port_move_member: For a nonnull destination, allocates a waitq link and jointly translates the receive port and port set, adds the selected set, then unlinks all other memberships while retaining that set. A null destination removes all memberships and reports `KERN_NOT_IN_SET` when none existed. Detached/unused links are freed after unlocking. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1403).
mach_port_request_notification: Validates the notification capability and whether its port type can receive notifications. The ID selects port-destroyed backup registration, no-senders registration/immediate delivery based on send count and make-send generation, or dead-name/send-possible request-table installation. Replacement rights and immediate delivery have distinct ownership paths; port policy can reject registration even when the receive right exists. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1514).
mach_port_insert_right: Validates a legal destination name, a port-right disposition and a live kernel port capability, then calls `ipc_object_copyout_name`. The lower copyout operation installs or merges the transferred right at the requested name subject to entry/right collisions and uref limits; the kernel port pointer is not itself a userspace name. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1659).
mach_port_extract_right: Checks the disposition and name, then uses `ipc_object_copyin` to extract the right as a kernel port plus resulting disposition. Only copying a send right from the current space passes the immovable-send allowance here. On success it reports `ipc_object_copyin_type`; invalid special names are errors rather than an exported dead name. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1698).
mach_port_get_attributes_from_user: Converts a readable space and dispatches the information flavor. The helper returns queue limits, receive status, request-table capacity, extended importance/guard status, or service throttle state, with flavor-specific count/name checks. Receive status exposes whether send rights exist and whether the port belongs to a set, not the set's kernel identity. The service-throttle branch requires a service port and has different count handling from the fixed-size branches. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1932).
mach_port_set_attributes: Dispatches by flavor under a translated receive-port lock. Queue-limit updates enforce `MACH_PORT_QLIMIT_MAX`; the DNREQUESTS_SIZE branch currently validates/looks up but does not resize. Temporary-owner/importance flavors change donation state and release/drop associated importance assertions after unlocking. Service throttling updates the service label; unsupported flavors and unsuitable port types fail. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1954).
task_set_port_space: The `table_entries` parameter is unused. The body rejects a null space and otherwise returns success, without reserving, growing or resizing the entry table. Its historical name is not evidence of current table-sizing behavior. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2256).
mach_port_get_srights: Requires a receive right, reads `ip_srights` under the port lock, then publishes that count after unlocking. This is the port's send-right reference count rather than the urefs held under one namespace name. Compare the separate `mach_port_get_refs` interface. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L105).
mach_port_space_info_from_user: Converts a readable space and collects namespace information plus an out-of-line entry array. Allocation occurs outside the space lock; the helper rechecks size and may drop/reacquire the lock between batches, so the entire array is not an atomic snapshot. It captures object pointer values without retaining the objects and hashes those values after unlocking; it does not dereference them then. Obsolete tree output is empty, and the wrapper releases the space reference. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L323), [collection/export](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L218).
mach_port_dnrequest_info: Translates a receive right and scans `ip_requests` while holding the port lock. Returns table capacity and the number of entries with a nonnull notification right, excluding the host-notify sentinel. An absent request table produces zero for both outputs. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L404).
mach_port_kernel_object: The historical kernel-object query remains a client declaration but the corresponding server slot is skipped. Follow the newer kobject query/description entries for current local inspection behavior; do not interpret this declaration as a callable receiver.
mach_port_insert_member: Preallocates a waitq link, jointly translates and locks the receive port and port set, then calls `ipc_mqueue_add_locked`. Unlocks both objects and frees a link that was not consumed. Existing membership and invalid rights are handled through the actual add/translation result, rather than replacing other memberships as `move_member` does. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2153).
mach_port_extract_member: Jointly translates/locks the receive port and named set, unlinks that specific waitq membership, unlocks both, and frees the detached link. A missing link produces `KERN_NOT_IN_SET`; other memberships are not removed by this entry. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2212).
mach_port_get_context_from_user: Converts the destination with the readable-space converter and calls the receive-right context helper. The helper returns zero for strictly guarded ports because the context is also the guard value; otherwise it copies `ip_context` under the port lock. The space reference is released after the call. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1161).
mach_port_set_context: Translates a receive right and updates `ip_context` under the port lock. Strict guarding prevents this overwrite: the function unlocks, records `kGUARD_EXC_SET_CONTEXT` and returns an error. Context is application-associated metadata, but it also participates in guard enforcement. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L1195).
mach_port_kobject_from_user: Delegates to `mach_port_kobject_description_from_user` with no description buffer. The common helper converts a readable namespace, accepts send/receive rights, derives an exported object type, and returns address zero in release builds or a hashed kernel address in development/debug builds. It does not grant access to the associated object. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L651).
mach_port_construct: Validates one port-type selection and unused flags, derives the label/type and entitlement/policy requirements, checks queue limits and optional render-server tracking, then allocates service/bootstrap/connection label state and the namespace port, passing any initial-send-right request as an allocation flag. After successful allocation the body enters its no-failure configuration phase: queue limit, donation/reply settings and guard/context are installed before unlocking. See [construction and policy](../../subsystems/ipc/guards-and-policy-enforcement.md). [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2420).
mach_port_destruct: Looks up the namespace entry with a write lock and delegates to `ipc_right_destruct`, which requires a receive right and a nonpositive send-right delta. The guard value is checked only when the port is guarded; unguarded receive rights can also be destructed. The helper adjusts send urefs, then removes receive ownership, potentially transferring it through a port-destroyed request rather than killing the endpoint. It releases the space lock and performs notification cleanup. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2698), [rights helper](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_right.c#L1664).
mach_port_guard: Translates and locks the receive right, maps the boolean strict option to `MPG_STRICT`, and invokes the shared guard helper. A nonzero existing context causes a guard exception/error; otherwise the helper stores the guard in `ip_context` and sets guarded/strict state. The outer wrapper releases the queue lock. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2743).
mach_port_unguard: Under a translated receive-port lock, checks that the port is guarded and the supplied value matches `ip_context`. Failure records the appropriate guard exception. Success clears the context and both guarded/strict flags; it does not destroy the name or remove any immovable-receive label state. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2796).
mach_port_space_basic_info: Read-locks an active IPC space, obtains its entry-table size and computes used entries from the free count, excluding entry zero. Returns the generation-number mask and zeroed reserved fields without allocating the full per-name array. Dead/null spaces fail. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L358).
mach_port_special_reply_port_reset_link: Development/debug builds require the current IPC space and the calling thread's exact special-reply receive port. They return `ip_srp_lost_link` and clear that diagnostic flag under the port lock. Other builds return `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; the operation does not reconstruct a lost synchronization link. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L662).
mach_port_guard_with_flags: Shares receive-right translation and the guard helper with the boolean API. The helper rejects a nonzero existing context, stores the guard/strict bit, and can transition the port label to immovable-receive state for `MPG_IMMOVABLE_RECEIVE`. Follow the actual helper rather than older comments about unsupported guard flag checks. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2845).
mach_port_swap_guard: Requires a guarded receive port, rejects strict guards, and compares the existing context with `old_guard`. Only after all three checks does it overwrite `ip_context` with `new_guard`. Each failed state check unlocks before recording the corresponding guard exception; this operation preserves guarded state. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2892).
mach_port_kobject_description_from_user: Converts a readable space and looks up a send/receive right. The common body reports a public object-type classification and optionally formats IOKit object, task-identity-token, named-memory-entry or thread-resume details. IOKit objects are retained before dropping the port lock for description work. Raw addresses are not exposed: release builds return zero and development/debug builds return a hash. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_debug.c#L629).
mach_port_is_connection_for_service: Requires a supported message-filter callback version, translates the service receive right and retains its sandbox label before unlocking. With no service label it returns policy ID zero. Otherwise it translates the connection port, retains an applicable connection label, and passes both to the filter callback, whose contract consumes those references. The filter implementation is an external policy boundary. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L2947).
mach_port_get_service_port_info: With `CONFIG_SERVICE_PORT_INFO`, translates a receive right and accepts service or bootstrap labels, copying their recorded information while protected. Other types fail with invalid capability. The configuration-disabled body always returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L3024).
mach_port_assert_attributes: Currently accepts only `MACH_PORT_GUARD_INFO`, checks the input count and receive right, then requires guarded state, strict guarding and the matching context value. Mismatch records a guard exception and returns invalid argument; success only verifies state and does not modify it. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/mach_port.c#L3078).
mach_voucher_extract_attr_content: Maps the key to the voucher's immutable value index; an unused value produces an empty successful output. Otherwise it finds the registered manager/control, rejects an absent manager, and calls `ivace_lookup_values`, whose current body returns exactly one handle for a present value. The manager's extraction callback receives that handle and the caller's capacity, and its status is returned directly. These bytes are manager-defined. [Implementation](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1668), [value lookup](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L515).
mach_voucher_extract_attr_recipe: Requires room for a recipe header after locating a present attribute, initializes key/command/previous-voucher fields and gives the remaining capacity to the manager extractor. On success it reports header plus actual content length. Missing attributes return zero length; insufficient header capacity returns `KERN_NO_SPACE`. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1737).
mach_voucher_extract_all_attr_recipes: Iterates voucher key indices, skips unused values and appends a header/content record per present attribute. Insufficient capacity or an extraction callback error stops the walk; only full completion writes the final used size. A missing manager is asserted against and, in the explicit fallback branch, skipped rather than returned as an error. The immutable voucher is unchanged. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1820).
mach_voucher_attr_command: Finds the manager/control for the requested key and resolves the voucher's value handles, then dispatches `ivam_command` with command number and input/output buffers. Each manager defines the actual command semantics and validation; the common voucher layer validates voucher/manager presence and supplies the associated values. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1972).
mach_voucher_debug_info: Development/debug builds translate the named send right, convert it to a referenced voucher, unlock the port, extract all recipes and release the voucher. Invalid names/types fail. The nondevelopment/nondebug body returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`, so a declaration alone does not imply recipe inspection is available. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1911).
mach_voucher_attr_control_get_values: Validates a nonnull control and voucher, takes the key index from the control and retrieves zero handles for an unused value or exactly one cached handle for a present value in the current `ivace_lookup_values` body. Zero requested output capacity returns success immediately. This is control-capability access to internal attribute values; the separate subsystem is not registered in `mig_e`. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L2036).
mach_voucher_attr_control_create_mach_vo: This historical declaration is skipped by the kernel-server profile and its subsystem is absent from `mig_e`; no same-symbol receiver is resolved. A distinct local helper, `ipc_voucher_attr_control_create_mach_voucher`, rejects a null control and passes its privilege plus kernel-form recipes to `ipc_create_mach_voucher_internal`. That helper does not establish a callable receiver for the `mach_` declaration. [Local kernel helper](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1595), [reserved server slots](../../../xnu/osfmk/mach/mach_voucher_attr_control.defs#L40).
mach_eventlink_create: Accepts only the current task and `MELC_OPTION_NO_COPYIN`. Allocation creates one shared base, two `IKOT_EVENTLINK` ports with send rights, two endpoint counters/association fields and a FIFO waitq. Returns both ports as the endpoint pair. Counter wait/signal operations use the separate BSD entries described in the syscall catalog. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_eventlink.c#L155).
mach_eventlink_destroy: Calls internal pair teardown and returns success unconditionally, including when teardown reports termination. Under the shared base lock at scheduler priority, teardown clears both associations/port pointers, forces wakeups and invalidates the waitq. After unlocking it deallocates only the local endpoint port, disables the remote port's kobject without destroying that port, releases associated thread references and drops both port-owned base references. [Wrapper and teardown](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_eventlink.c#L239).
mach_eventlink_associate: Rejects nonzero copyin addresses/masks and incompatible thread/associate-on-wait combinations. Under the shared eventlink lock at scheduler priority, requires an active unassociated endpoint and stores either a retained thread or the wildcard sentinel consumed on wait. Reassociation returns `KERN_NAME_EXISTS`. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_eventlink.c#L361).
mach_eventlink_disassociate: Requires `MELD_OPTION_NONE` and an active associated endpoint. Clears `el_thread` and forces a wake while holding the base lock, then restores priority and releases the retained thread unless it was the wildcard sentinel. Disassociation therefore also affects an already waiting caller. [`Implementation`](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_eventlink.c#L428).
